## About me

Hi! I am Zana, a PhD student in the Department of Oncology-Pathology at Karolinska Institutet, based at BioClinicum in Solna.

<!-- Write a few sentences about yourself here: your background, how you ended up in cancer research, what you enjoy outside the lab... -->

## My research

My PhD project is about **immune evasion in Merkel cell carcinoma**, a rare and aggressive skin cancer. Immunotherapy with PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitors works very well for some patients, but not for all of them. I am trying to understand why some tumours do not respond.

<!-- Add more detail if you want: methods you use, which data you work with, why reproducible bioinformatics matters for your project... -->

## Why this blog?

I started this blog during the course *Reproducible Research in Bioinformatics and Computational Biology* (September 2026). It is a report of what I did during the course, and a notebook I can come back to whenever I need to remember how to use Pixi, containers, Nextflow or nf-core.
